hints.title: Filtering by Content Length
hints.text: Filter the tweet rows based on content length.

hints.title: Character Count vs Byte Count
hints.text: use the length function that counts characters rather than bytes to handle multi-byte characters accurately.

hints.title: Applying Strict Inequality
hints.text: apply char_length(content) strictly greater than 15 in the where clause and select tweet_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT tweet_id
FROM Tweets
WHERE CHAR_LENGTH(content) > 15;
```

complexity.notes: Linear table scan filtering tweets whose character length strictly exceeds 15.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Using byte-length functions like LENGTH in UTF-8 environments produces inaccurate character counts for non-ASCII characters.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Scanning the table and evaluating character length takes linear O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand the distinction between CHAR_LENGTH (characters) and LENGTH (bytes) in SQL.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def invalid_tweets(tweets: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = tweets[tweets['content'].str.len() > 15]
    return df[['tweet_id']]
